name: Light Salmon-Orange
lede: Light Salmon-Orange is a soft, pale orange filed three ways in our sources: as a modifier on [[light-salmon|Light Salmon]], as a Ridgway hue from 1912, and as the Japanese traditional color Usugaki, "pale persimmon."

sections.title: Three records, one hue
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 atlas plates this hue at plate II, hue 11, tone d, and the ISCC-NBS system separately filed it in 1955 as block 53 [1]. Our color graph files the same approximate hue, sourced to Wikipedia's list of traditional Japanese colors, as *Usugaki* (薄柿), literally "pale persimmon," one of a family of persimmon-dyed browns and oranges named for the fruit [2]. In our data it also sits in the "family word" position under [[light-salmon|Light Salmon]], the X11 web color, measuring a touch lighter and less saturated (lightness 78 against 75, chroma 42 against 47) [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[salmon-color|Salmon Color]], 2.8 units away and duller, with [[light-orange|Light Orange]] close behind at 3.8, more vivid [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pale orange in 34 of 23,781 paintings (0.14 percent, as photographed), rarer than 60 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It most often plays an accent, in 62 percent of its strongest matches, and peaks in paintings from the 1800s [3]. The earliest dated match runs to 1516, by Raphael, 396 years before Ridgway's 1912 record; a floor, not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].

origin.named_after: a descriptive modifier: light + Salmon-Orange; also the Japanese traditional color Usugaki, "pale persimmon"
